conventions.convention: Levels start at zero; Q_{-1}=0, Δ_0=Q_0, and Δ_l=Q_l−Q_{l−1}. The selected Simpson hierarchy uses 2^{l+1} panels on [0,1], with three baseline nodes.
An admissible Smolyak set is finite, nonempty, downward closed, and contains zero; cubature sums its tensor details. Work counts the entire distinct node union.
Canonical node keys agree exactly iff the real node tuples agree. Nodes with zero combined weight are still evaluated and counted; arithmetic and comparisons are exact.
A nonnegative multi-index sum is the supremum of all finite subsums, provided those subsums are bounded above; no enumeration is required.

For S={j_1<…<j_k}, D_S applies fourth derivatives in increasing coordinate order. Every D_S, including D_empty=f, is continuous on the closed cube, with one-sided endpoint derivatives and finite bounds M_S.

The adaptive budget counts distinct samples for both accepted and candidate surpluses. An undersized baseline budget returns an empty accepted set and no cubature value. Surpluses are indicators, without an error-certificate claim.
Polynomial exactness uses supplied nondecreasing one-dimensional degree bounds and the least levels attaining the required degrees; node counts do not determine exactness.

The explicit work/error theorem uses the Simpson hierarchy, d≥1 and n≥2d, natural logarithms, and dimension-dependent constants. The four-dimensional example instead uses Clenshaw–Curtis degrees one and two.

load_bearing.statement: A nested hierarchy has X_{l−1}⊆X_l, Q_{−1}=0, Δ_0=Q_0 and Δ_l=Q_l−Q_{l−1}; the selected dyadic Simpson rule is Q_l(g)=Q_S(g;0,1,2^{l+1}). Tensor functionals multiply coordinate weights.
For an admissible finite downward-closed Λ, Q_Λ(f)=Σ_{l∈Λ}δ_l(f), and W(Λ) is the cardinality of the union of its tensor-level node sets; combined weights may be negative or zero.

Under its continuous sequential mixed fourth-derivative hypotheses, |δ_l(f)|≤M_{S(l)}(17/2880)^{|S(l)|}16^{−Σ_{j∈S(l)}l_j}; every finite absolute-detail subsum is at most Σ_{S⊆[d]}M_S(17/43200)^{|S|}.
For d≥1 and terminal levels m_j≥0, the sum of tensor details over 0≤l_j≤m_j equals Q_{m_1}⊗⋯⊗Q_{m_d}.
For d≥1 and continuous f:[0,1]^d→R, the selected dyadic tensor composite-Simpson rules satisfy Q_L^{⊗d}(f)→I_d(f).
For continuous f, tensor-rule convergence to I_d(f) and absolute detail summability imply |I_d(f)−Q_Λ(f)|≤Σ_{l∉Λ}|δ_l(f)| for every finite downward-closed Λ containing zero.

For the Simpson hierarchy, d≥1, n≥2d, and the stated mixed-derivative class, the exact minimal-level node count satisfies 2^n binom(n−1,d−1)≤W_{n,d}≤D_d2^n(n+1)^{d−1}; the error is at most T_d‖f‖_{mix,d}16^{−n}(n+1)^{d−1}≤C_d‖f‖_{mix,d}W_{n,d}^{−4}(log(2+W_{n,d}))^{5(d−1)}.

concerns.concern: The Definition begins 'Let Q:[0,1]→R be a finite quadrature functional' but immediately defines Q(g)=Σ_i w_i g(x_i). Its arguments are functions g:[0,1]→R, rather than points of [0,1]. The displayed domain has the wrong type; the subsequent formula makes the intended functional unambiguous.

The Example says the pure fourth derivative 'fails to exist along the diagonal'. Under the stated one-sided endpoint convention this needs an interior qualifier: at (0,0), the fixed-y section is x³ on [0,1], and at (1,1) it is (1−x)³, so their fourth endpoint derivatives exist and equal zero. Step 1.1 correctly proves failure for y∈(0,1); the example's regularity counterexample remains valid.

The exactness theorem uses cubic exactness without asserting increasing Simpson polynomial degree.

Read the quadrature definition and exactness statement. Read the Gaussian-rule and tensor-rule definitions and the exactness/positive-weights theorem. The signed-weight example uses positivity only for valid positive-measure moment data and explicitly disclaims Gaussian exactness for its high-degree polynomial.
